title: Staged Pin Eviction & Regional Variant Escalation with Observability Hooks
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Goal: design and implement a staged eviction and fallback mechanism for model version pins that minimizes customer disruption during deprecations or regional capacity disruptions. This ticket covers: 1) pin metadata TTL and staged eviction windows, 2) a priority escalation path for regional/model-variant fallback, 3) telemetry hooks and SLO signals that drive automated grace windows, and 4) compatibility checks for variant fallbacks (quantization/hardware compatibility enforcement). Success criteria: (a) zero user-visible 5xxs during a controlled pin eviction across 3 customers in staging, (b) bounded tail latency increase <= 15% for affected requests during an eviction grace window, and (c) clear rollback path and audit trail for every automated fallback. Non-goals: making permanent changes to pricing, or modifying model catalog discovery flows beyond adding compatibility metadata fields.
acceptance_criteria: Pinned model can be marked for staged eviction with a 3-tier grace window (soft, warm, hard)
Routing layer performs regional variant escalation based on configurable priority list and compatibility flags
Telemetry emits pinned_eviction.{soft|warm|hard} events and SLO breach signals to Console dashboards
Automated fallback must create an audit log entry and a reversible rollout record visible in Console
Integration tests that simulate regional GPU exhaustion produce deterministic fallback decisions and no runtime crashes
design_notes: We propose adding two fields to pin metadata: eviction_window (enum: soft,warm,hard) and variant_priority (ordered list of model-variant ids). When a pin enters 'soft' window, clients receive warning headers (x-rw-pin-warning) and Console shows a countdown. 'Warm' triggers background prefix cache warming for target variants and a split-traffic canary (5%). 'Hard' triggers full automatic failover to highest-priority compatible variant. Compatibility checks will validate tokenizer, max_seq_len, and quantization profile; incompatible variants are skipped with a clear rationale logged. Observability: emit events at each state transition, include tokenized latency deltas, and surface affected customer IDs and request hashes for postmortem. Rollback: a one-click revert from Console that re-applies pin and issues a rollback event. Tradeoffs: increased metadata size and slightly more complex routing logic vs. reduced customer outages during deprecations.
implementation_steps: Schema: extend pin metadata model (DB migration + default values)
Routing: implement staged eviction state machine in router and policy engine
Compatibility: build a fast in-memory compatibility cache populated at model onboarding
Observability: add eviction events, Console panels, and runbooks
E2E tests: deterministic simulation harness for multi-region capacity loss
Rollout: feature-flagged rollout to staging -> canary customers -> all customers
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: false-positive compatibility failures block fallback. Mitigation: fall back to conservative skip-logging and include a manual override path for SEs.
Risk: cache-warming traffic causes additional cost spikes. Mitigation: cap warm-up qps and use sampled requests for warming priority prefixes.
Risk: UI confusion about pin state. Mitigation: add explicit statuses (Active, Warning, Warming, Evicted) and contextual help in Console.
Risk: cascading fallbacks across regions. Mitigation: implement global cooldown tokens and per-customer rate limits for automated evictions.
